questions.question: Pravin has ₹1224 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Rishi and Shan and asked them to invest it at 4% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Rishi and Shan got same amount after 15 and 16 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Pravin give to Shan?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For equal amounts in Compound Interest, the principal ratio relies on the difference in time periods.

Ratio (Rishi : Shan) = (1 + R/100)T² − T¹ : 1

⇒ Rishi : Shan = (1 + 4/100)¹⁶ − ¹⁵ : 1 = (26/25) : 1 = 26 : 25

⇒ Total parts = 26 + 25 = 51 parts → ₹1224

⇒ Shan's share = (25 / 51) × 1224 = 600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount Pravin has = ₹1224

Rate of interest (R) = 4% compounded annually

Time for Rishi (T₁) = 15 years

Time for Shan (T₂) = 16 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount in Compound Interest: A = P(1 + R/100)T

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

 
 
 Total Sum = ₹1224
 
 
 

 

 
 
 
 Rishi's Share
 15 Years @ 4% CI

 
 
 Shan's Share
 16 Years @ 4% CI
 
 
 

 

 
 
 
 Equal Final Amounts

**Calculations:**

Let the initial amount given to Rishi be PR and to Shan be PS.

⇒ Total sum = PR + PS = 1224

⇒ Final amount of Rishi = PR × (1 + 4/100)¹⁵

⇒ Final amount of Shan = PS × (1 + 4/100)¹⁶

Since the amounts received by both are equal after their respective periods:

⇒ PR × (1 + 1/25)¹⁵ = PS × (1 + 1/25)¹⁶

⇒ PR × (26/25)¹⁵ = PS × (26/25)¹⁶

Dividing both sides by (26/25)¹⁵:

⇒ PR = PS × (26/25)

⇒ PR / PS = 26 / 25

⇒ PR : PS = 26 : 25

⇒ Total parts in ratio = 26 + 25 = 51 parts

⇒ 51 parts = ₹1224

⇒ 1 part = 1224 ÷ 51 = ₹24

⇒ Amount given to Shan (PS) = 25 parts = 25 × 24 = 600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Interest Rate

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate is halved (R/2) and the time period is doubled (2T). The formula becomes A = P(1 + R/200)²T.

Difference Between CI and SI

For 2 years on the same principal P at rate R%, the difference is D = P(R/100)². For 3 years, the difference is D = P(R/100)²(3 + R/100).

Successive Compound Interest

If the rate of interest is different for different years (R₁, R₂, R₃), the total amount is calculated sequentially as A = P(1 + R₁/100)(1 + R₂/100)(1 + R₃/100).

questions.question: If x varies indirectly to y² and if x = 78, y = 11, then find the value of x when y = 2.2.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since x ∝ 1/y², the ratio of change in x is the inverse ratio of change in y².

y decreases from 11 to 2.2, which means it becomes 1/5 of its initial value.

Thus, y² decreases by a factor of (1/5)² = 1/25.

Due to inverse variation, x must increase by a factor of 25.

New value of x = 78 × 25 = 1950.

**∴ The correct answer is 1950.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x₁ = 78, y₁ = 11

y₂ = 2.2

x varies inversely as y²

**Formula Used:**

x₁ × y₁² = x₂ × y₂²

 
 State 1
 y = 11
 y² = 121
 x = 78

 
 State 2
 y = 2.2
 y² = 4.84
 x = ?

 

 y² ÷ 25

 

 x × 25

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 78 × (11)² = x₂ × (2.2)²

⇒ 78 × 121 = x₂ × 4.84

⇒ x₂ = (78 × 121) ÷ 4.84

⇒ x₂ = 78 × (121 ÷ 4.84)

⇒ x₂ = 78 × 25

⇒ x₂ = 1950

**∴ The correct answer is 1950.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Variation

When two variables change in the same proportion. Formula: x ∝ y ⇒ x = ky, where k is a constant.

Inverse (Indirect) Variation

When one variable increases while the other decreases proportionally. Formula: x ∝ 1/y ⇒ x × y = k.

Joint Variation

When a variable varies directly or inversely with multiple variables simultaneously. For example: x ∝ y × z ⇒ x = k × y × z.

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 18 days, B and C can do the same work in 32 days and A and C can do the same in 52 days. The time taken by A, B and C together to do the work is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Total Work = LCM of 18, 32, and 52 = 3744 units.

Combined 1-day work (efficiency): (A + B) = 3744 ÷ 18 = 208, (B + C) = 3744 ÷ 32 = 117, (C + A) = 3744 ÷ 52 = 72.

Adding them all gives 2 × (A + B + C) = 208 + 117 + 72 = 397 units.

Efficiency of (A + B + C) = 397 ÷ 2 units/day.

Time taken by them together = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency = 3744 ÷ (397 ÷ 2) = 7488 ÷ 397 = 18 ³⁴²/₃₉₇ days.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 ³⁴²/₃₉₇ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A and B to complete the work = 18 days

Time taken by B and C to complete the work = 32 days

Time taken by A and C to complete the work = 52 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of Time

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Total Time Taken = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of (A + B) + (B + C) + (C + A) = 208 + 117 + 72

⇒ 2 × (A + B + C) = 397

⇒ Efficiency of (A + B + C) = 397 ÷ 2

⇒ Time taken by A, B, and C together = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of (A + B + C)

⇒ Time taken = 7488 ÷ 397 = 18 ³⁴²/₃₉₇ days

**∴ The correct answer is 18 ³⁴²/₃₉₇ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Efficiency Rule

If A can do a piece of work in x days and B can do it in y days, their combined time is (x × y) ÷ (x + y) days.

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in the ratio of the total work done. If the time spent by workers is constant, wages are directly proportional to their efficiencies.

Pipes and Cisterns

Similar to the time and work model, but an outlet pipe performs negative work, effectively subtracting from the total efficiency.

questions.question: Bhanu travels from City A to City B. If Bhanu drives his car at (3)/(7) of his normal speed, then he reaches City B 28 minutes late. Find the time (in minutes) that Bhanu would have taken to travel from City A to City B if he drove at his normal speed.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the new speed is 3/7 of the normal speed, the Speed Ratio (Normal : New) = 7 : 3.

Time is inversely proportional to speed, so Time Ratio (Normal : New) = 3 : 7.

Difference in time ratio parts = 7 − 3 = 4 parts.

Given delay is 28 minutes ⇒ 4 parts = 28 minutes ⇒ 1 part = 7 minutes.

Normal time = 3 parts = 3 × 7 = 21 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 21 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

New speed = 3/7 of normal speed.

Time delay = 28 minutes late.

 Normal Case
 Speed = S, Time = T

 
 New Case
 Speed = 3S/7, Time = T + 28

 S × T = (3S/7) × (T + 28)

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the normal speed be S and normal time be T minutes.

⇒ Distance D = S × T

⇒ New speed = 3S/7

⇒ New time = T + 28

⇒ New Distance = (3S/7) × (T + 28)

⇒ Since distance is constant: S × T = (3S/7) × (T + 28)

⇒ Canceling S from both sides: T = (3/7) × (T + 28)

⇒ 7T = 3T + 84

⇒ 4T = 84

⇒ T = 21 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 21 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportionality of Speed and Time

When the distance covered is constant, speed is inversely proportional to the time taken. If speed becomes a/b times, the time taken becomes b/a times.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed = |S₁ − S₂|. In opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

Average Speed

When equal distances are covered at speeds a and b, Average Speed = (2ab) ÷ (a + b). If equal times are spent, Average Speed = (a + b) ÷ 2.

questions.question: Shivam has two grandsons Rupesh and Mandar. 12 year old Rupesh gets some money from Shivam’s wealth and 13 year old Mandar gets rest of the money. But Rupesh and Mandar will get money only when they turn 23 years old. Till then the money is in a bank getting interest at rate 8% compounded annually. When both turn 23, they receive the same amount. How much had Shivam given Mandar (in ₹) initially, if total money with Shivam was ₹24700?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time difference between Rupesh and Mandar = 13 − 12 = 1 year.

Rate of interest = 8% = 2/25 → Multiplying factor = 27/25.

Since Mandar has less time, he gets a larger share. Ratio of Mandar's to Rupesh's share = 27¹ : 25¹ = 27 : 25.

Total parts = 27 + 25 = 52 parts.

Mandar's share = (27 ÷ 52) × 24700 = ₹12825.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12825.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Money = ₹24,700

Rate of Interest = 8% compounded annually

Age of Rupesh = 12 years, Age of Mandar = 13 years

Target age for equality = 23 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount in CI, A = P(1 + R/100)T

 
 Rupesh (12 yrs):
 Principal R
 
• 
 

 11 Years
 Amount A

 
 Mandar (13 yrs):
 Principal M
 
• 
 

 10 Years
 Amount A

 Amounts are EQUAL at Age 23

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time for Rupesh = 23 − 12 = 11 years

⇒ Time for Mandar = 23 − 13 = 10 years

⇒ Let the amount given to Rupesh be R and Mandar be M.

⇒ Amount of Rupesh = Amount of Mandar

⇒ R(1 + 8/100)¹¹ = M(1 + 8/100)¹⁰

⇒ R(108/100)¹¹ = M(108/100)¹⁰

⇒ M / R = (108/100)¹

⇒ M / R = 27 / 25

⇒ Total ratio units = 27 + 25 = 52 units

⇒ 52 units = 24700

⇒ 1 unit = 24700 ÷ 52 = 475

⇒ Mandar's initial amount = 27 units

⇒ Mandar's initial amount = 27 × 475 = 12825

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12825.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Distribution of Wealth with Compound Interest

When money is divided between two people such that they get equal amounts at a certain age, the person who has less time to invest must receive a larger principal.

Compound Interest Formula

Amount, A = P(1 + R/100)N, where P is principal, R is rate of interest per annum, and N is the number of years.

Ratio of Principals in CI

If two parts P₁ and P₂ amount to the same value in T₁ and T₂ years respectively, then their initial investment ratio is given by P₁/P₂ = (1 + R/100)T²−T¹.

questions.question: The average of 21 numbers is 74. The average of the first 11 numbers is 72.8 and that of the last 11 numbers is 77.2. If the 10th number is five less than the 11th number and if 10th and 11th numbers are excluded, then what is the average of the remaining numbers? (correct to nearest integer)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

11th number = Average + 11 × (Deviation of first 11) + 11 × (Deviation of last 11)

11th number = 74 + 11 × (72.8 − 74) + 11 × (77.2 − 74) = 74 + 22 = 96

10th number = 96 − 5 = 91

Total deviation of 10th and 11th numbers from average = (96 − 74) + (91 − 74) = +39

Since the excluded numbers are 39 above average, the average of the remaining 19 numbers will decrease.

New average = 74 − (39 ÷ 19) = 74 − 2.05 = 71.95 ≈ 72

**∴ The correct answer is 72.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total numbers = 21, Average = 74

Average of first 11 numbers = 72.8

Average of last 11 numbers = 77.2

 
 
 First 11: 11 × 72.8 = 800.8

 
 
 Last 11: 11 × 77.2 = 849.2

 
 
• 
 
•

• 

 
 Total 21 Numbers: 21 × 74 = 1554

 
 
 
 

 
 10th = 91
 
• 

 11th = 96

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of all 21 numbers = 21 × 74 = 1554

⇒ Sum of first 11 numbers = 11 × 72.8 = 800.8

⇒ Sum of last 11 numbers = 11 × 77.2 = 849.2

⇒ By adding the first 11 and last 11, the 11th number is counted twice.

⇒ 11th number = (800.8 + 849.2) − 1554

⇒ 11th number = 1650 − 1554 = 96

⇒ 10th number = 96 − 5 = 91

⇒ Sum of excluded numbers (10th and 11th) = 96 + 91 = 187

⇒ Sum of remaining 19 numbers = 1554 − 187 = 1367

⇒ Average of remaining 19 numbers = 1367 ÷ 19 = 71.947 ≈ 72

**∴ The correct answer is 72.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Overlapping Concept in Averages

When a sequence is divided into two overlapping parts, the common item is counted twice. It can be isolated using: Overlapping Item = (Sum of Part 1 + Sum of Part 2) − Total Sum.

Impact of Excluded Items

If the values removed from a group are greater than the original average, the new average of the remaining items will decrease. Change in average = Total deviation of removed items ÷ Remaining number of items.

Combined Average

When groups are combined, the new average is given by A = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the number of items and A is their respective average.
</p

questions.question: A soap company produces two kinds of soaps having weight 500 gm and 650 gm, respectively. If 200 soaps of the first kind and 300 soaps of second the kind were produced, then what is the weighted average weight (in gm) of the soaps?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of soap quantities = 200 : 300 = 2 : 3

Let assumed average weight be 500 gm.

Deviation of second soap = 650 − 500 = +150 gm

Net average change = (150 × 3) ÷ (2 + 3) = 450 ÷ 5 = +90 gm

Actual Average = 500 + 90 = 590 gm

**∴ The correct answer is 590 gm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Weight of 1st soap (W₁) = 500 gm

Quantity of 1st soap (N₁) = 200

Weight of 2nd soap (W₂) = 650 gm

Quantity of 2nd soap (N₂) = 300

**Formula Used:**

Weighted Average = (W₁ × N₁ + W₂ × N₂) ÷ (N₁ + N₂)

 
• 
 
 
 

 
 
 500 gm
 650 gm
 Avg: 590
 
 Qty: 200
 Qty: 300
 
 

 

 Diff: 90
 Diff: 60

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total weight of 1st soap = 500 × 200 = 1,00,000 gm

⇒ Total weight of 2nd soap = 650 × 300 = 1,95,000 gm

⇒ Total quantity = 200 + 300 = 500

⇒ Total combined weight = 1,00,000 + 1,95,000 = 2,95,000 gm

⇒ Weighted Average = 2,95,000 ÷ 500

⇒ Weighted Average = 590 gm

**∴ The correct answer is 590 gm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

Used when elements in different groups have varying quantities. Formula: Aw = (x₁w₁ + x₂w₂) ÷ (w₁ + w₂).

Alligation Rule

A quicker method to find the ratio in which two components are mixed. Quantity Ratio = (Dearer − Mean) : (Mean − Cheaper).

Deviation Method for Averages

Select an assumed mean, calculate total deviations for all items, and distribute this net deviation equally over total items to find the actual average.
</p

**Given:**

LCM of the two numbers = 140

HCF of the two numbers = 5

First number = 35

**Formula Used:**

First Number × Second Number = LCM × HCF

 
 1st Num × 2nd Num

 =

 
 LCM × HCF

 
 35 × ?

 =

 
 140 × 5

**Calculations:**

⇒ 35 × Second Number = 140 × 5

⇒ 35 × Second Number = 700

⇒ Second Number = 700 ÷ 35

⇒ Second Number = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and HCF of Fractions

LCM of fractions = LCM of numerators ÷ HCF of denominators. HCF of fractions = HCF of numerators ÷ LCM of denominators.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their HCF is 1. The LCM of two co-prime numbers is always equal to their product.

HCF as a Factor

The HCF of given numbers is always a perfect divisor (factor) of their LCM.
</p

questions.question: Find the area of a triangle, whose sides are 6 cm, 0.08 m and 4 cm.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert all sides to the same unit: 0.08 m = 8 cm.

The sides are 6 cm, 8 cm, and 4 cm. Semi-perimeter (s) = (6 + 8 + 4) ÷ 2 = 9 cm.

Using direct Heron's formula: Area = √(9 × 3 × 1 × 5).

Area = √135 = 3√15 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 3√15 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Side a = 6 cm

⇒ Side b = 0.08 m

⇒ Side c = 4 cm

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Heron's formula: Area = √(s × (s − a) × (s − b) × (s − c))

⇒ Semi-perimeter, s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2

 

 8 cm (0.08 m)
 6 cm
 4 cm
 
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, convert all lengths to centimeters to maintain consistent units.

⇒ Side b = 0.08 m = 0.08 × 100 = 8 cm

⇒ Find the semi-perimeter (s):

⇒ s = (6 + 8 + 4) ÷ 2

⇒ s = 18 ÷ 2 = 9 cm

⇒ Now, substitute the values into Heron's formula:

⇒ Area = √(9 × (9 − 6) × (9 − 8) × (9 − 4))

⇒ Area = √(9 × 3 × 1 × 5)

⇒ Area = √135

⇒ Area = √(9 × 15) = 3√15 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 3√15 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Heron's Formula

Used to find the area of a scalene triangle when all three sides are known: Area = √(s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)).

Area of an Equilateral Triangle

For a triangle with all equal sides (length a), the area is calculated directly using: Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × a².

Area of a Right-Angled Triangle

When the base and perpendicular height are given: Area = (1 ÷ 2) × Base × Height.

questions.question:
Which of the following numbers will come in the place of x in the given equation?

0.3 : 4.8 : : 0.2 : x
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In the proportion a : b : : c : d, the ratio multiplier is constant.

Here, the first term 0.3 is multiplied by 16 to get the second term 4.8 (since 4.8 ÷ 0.3 = 16).

Applying the exact same multiplier to the third term 0.2:

x = 0.2 × 16 = 3.2

**∴ The correct answer is 3.2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

0.3 : 4.8 : : 0.2 : x

**Formula Used:**

For any proportion a : b : : c : d, the product of extremes is equal to the product of means.

⇒ a × d = b × c

 
 0.3
 
 :

 
 4.8

 ::

 
 0.2

 :

 
 x

 

 Product of Means

 

 Product of Extremes
 
 0.3 × x = 4.8 × 0.2

**Calculations:**

⇒ 0.3 × x = 4.8 × 0.2

⇒ 0.3x = 0.96

⇒ x = 0.96 ÷ 0.3

⇒ x = 3.2

**∴ The correct answer is 3.2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Fourth Proportional

If a : b : : c : d, then d is called the fourth proportional to a, b, and c. It is calculated as d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Third Proportional

If a : b : : b : c, then c is called the third proportional to a and b. It is calculated as c = b² ÷ a.

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is given by √(a × b).
</p

questions.question: Find the value of [(29times 13)times left{3÷3times ((18-14))/(4)right}]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

We need to find the value of the following expression:

**[ (29 × 13) × {3 ÷ 3 × (18 - 14) / 4} ]**

First, simplify the inner expression:

18 - 14 = 4

Now, substitute into the expression:

**[ (29 × 13) × {3 ÷ 3 × 4 / 4} ]**

Next, simplify inside the brackets:

3 ÷ 3 = 1

4 / 4 = 1

So, 1 × 1 = 1, and the expression becomes:

**[ (29 × 13) × 1 ]**

Now, calculate 29 × 13:

29 × 13 = 377

**Therefore, the value of the expression is 377.**

questions.question: A man sold an article for ₹219, there by gaining 9.5%. The cost of the article (in ₹) was:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Fractional value of 9.5% = 9.5 ÷ 100 = 19 ÷ 200.

This means if Cost Price (CP) is 200 units, the Profit is 19 units.

Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit = 200 + 19 = 219 units.

Given SP is 219 units = ₹219 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹1.

Cost Price = 200 units × 1 = ₹200.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = ₹219

Gain percentage = 9.5%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = [100 ÷ (100 + Gain%)] × SP

 
 CP = 100%
 
 Profit = 9.5%
 

 SP = 109.5% = ₹219

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = [100 ÷ (100 + 9.5)] × 219

⇒ CP = (100 ÷ 109.5) × 219

⇒ CP = (1000 ÷ 1095) × 219

⇒ CP = (200 ÷ 219) × 219

⇒ CP = 200 × 1

⇒ CP = 200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Calculation

When an article is sold at a loss, the Cost Price can be calculated as: CP = [100 ÷ (100 − Loss%)] × SP.

Marked Price and Discount

Selling Price can also be determined from Marked Price after allowing a discount: SP = MP × [(100 − Discount%) ÷ 100].

Successive Profit/Loss

For successive changes of x% and y%, the net percentage change is given by the effective percentage formula: Net % = x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100.

4% of x = 108

Percentage formula: {Percentage} = frac{{Part}}{{Whole}} times 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ (4)/(100) times x = 108

⇒ (4x)/(100) = 108

⇒ (x)/(25) = 108

⇒ x = 108 × 25

⇒ x = 2700

questions.question: Which scheme provides the highest discount among the options given?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective discount formula: D = x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100.

Comparing the total sum (x + y) for all options: Option 1 (20%), Option 2 (16%), Option 3 (10%), Option 4 (19%).

Option 1 has the highest sum, so it naturally provides the maximum effective discount.

Effective discount for Option 1 = 10 + 10 − (10 × 10) ÷ 100 = 19%.

Effective discount for Option 4 = 8 + 11 − (8 × 11) ÷ 100 = 18.12%.

**∴ The correct answer is Two successive discounts of 10% each.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Four different successive discount schemes to compare.

**Formula Used:**

Effective Discount = x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100

 Effective Discount Comparison
 
 10% & 10%
 
 19.00%

 8% & 8%
 
 15.36%

 5% & 5%
 
 9.75%

 8% & 11%
 
 18.12%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Scheme 1 effective discount = 10 + 10 − (10 × 10) ÷ 100 = 20 − 1 = 19%

⇒ Scheme 2 effective discount = 8 + 8 − (8 × 8) ÷ 100 = 16 − 0.64 = 15.36%

⇒ Scheme 3 effective discount = 5 + 5 − (5 × 5) ÷ 100 = 10 − 0.25 = 9.75%

⇒ Scheme 4 effective discount = 8 + 11 − (8 × 11) ÷ 100 = 19 − 0.88 = 18.12%

⇒ Comparing all the calculated effective discounts: 19% > 18.12% > 15.36% > 9.75%

⇒ Scheme 1 provides the highest effective discount.

**∴ The correct answer is Two successive discounts of 10% each.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

When two consecutive discounts of x% and y% are applied on a product, the effective single discount is always given by: D = x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100.

Comparing Discounts with the Same Sum

If two different pairs of successive discounts add up to the same total sum, the pair with the maximum difference between the two percentage values always provides the highest effective discount to the customer.

Marked Price and Selling Price

Discount is fundamentally always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). The final Selling Price (SP) after an effective discount of D% is calculated as: SP = MP × (100 − D) ÷ 100.

Buy X Get Y Free

This is another popular promotional discount scheme. The effective discount percentage here is calculated simply as: Discount % = (Free Items ÷ Total Items) × 100.
</p
